beatbox.host.no_bundle.title: The interface has not been built
beatbox.host.no_bundle.body: BeatBox renders a bundle that is committed to the repository, and there is none at {path}. Build it once and this window will open normally:
beatbox.host.no_disk: No disk to start from. Choose one you already have.
beatbox.host.no_agent: The machine is not answering yet. Wait a minute; if it keeps saying this, install the guest agent on its disk.
beatbox.host.guest_went: The machine closed suddenly (QEMU ended with code {code}).
beatbox.host.guest_shut_down: The machine was shut down from inside.
beatbox.host.guest_killed: The machine was closed by force by this computer's system, almost always because memory ran out. Give it less memory or close other programs.
beatbox.host.not_enough_memory: It wants {wanted} GB and only {free} GB are free. Give it less, or close other programs.
beatbox.host.guest_lost: BeatBox lost track of this machine while it was closed. It may still be running, or it may be gone.
beatbox.host.fixed_setting: {setting} is fixed once a host sandbox exists: its disk of its own is built on it.
beatbox.screen.host.machine.title: Machines
beatbox.screen.host.machine.blurb: A machine of your own, with a kernel of its own, that you can throw away. Point BeatBox at a disk you already have; it never writes to it.
beatbox.host.traffic_unreadable: The traffic recording could not be read: {detail}
beatbox.screen.host.pen.title: USB drive
beatbox.screen.host.pen.blurb: Take files from this computer into the machine, as if you plugged in a pen drive. The machine can only read it — it can never change or delete your files.
beatbox.host_pages.no_machines: There are no machines yet. Make one first.
beatbox.processes.end_sure: End {name}? Anything unsaved in it is lost.
beatbox.pen.title: The pen
beatbox.pen.pick: Choose the folder to put on the pen
beatbox.pen.how: Choose a folder on this computer: everything in it shows up inside the machine as a pen drive called “BEATBOX PEN”. Up to 500 MB.
beatbox.pen.in: Plugged in, with this folder on it:
beatbox.pen.inside: Inside the machine it is the pen drive called “BEATBOX PEN”. If it does not open by itself, look for it in the file manager.
beatbox.pen.safe: Read-only: the machine can look at these files and copy them, but nothing it does can change or delete them on this computer.
beatbox.pen.off: {name} is off. Start it to plug in a pen.
beatbox.pen.not_this_one: A machine marked as dangerous cannot take a pen.
beatbox.host.bad_pid: “{pid}” is not a process that can be ended.
beatbox.host.kill_refused: Process {pid} could not be ended — it may have finished already.
beatbox.host.pen_too_big: That folder holds more than a pen can: {limit} MB at most.
beatbox.host.no_uefi: This machine needs UEFI firmware for QEMU (OVMF). Install it with: {command}
beatbox.host.no_uefi_vars: The machine's UEFI settings could not be made: {detail}
beatbox.host.ova_is_an_archive: An .ova is a package, not a disk: take the disk out of it first (New machine offers to).
beatbox.pen.about: Take files from this computer into {name}, as if you plugged in a pen drive. It can only read them — it can never change or delete your files.
beatbox.screen.host.commands.title: Commands
beatbox.screen.host.commands.blurb: Run things inside a machine without touching its screen.
beatbox.screen.host.watchers.title: Watchers
beatbox.screen.host.watchers.blurb: Commands that keep running inside a machine, and tell you when something changes.
beatbox.commands.about: Run things inside {name} without touching its screen. Pick one from the library or type your own; it goes in through the guest agent and the answer comes back here.
beatbox.commands.no_agent: Commands need the guest agent in the machine and “Let BeatBox reach inside it” on in its settings.
beatbox.commands.off: {name} is off. Start it to run anything inside it.
beatbox.commands.built.uptime: How long it has been up
beatbox.commands.nothing_yet: Nothing has run yet. Pick a command and press Run.
beatbox.commands.typed: Anything — it runs inside {name}, not here
beatbox.commands.name: Call it
beatbox.commands.blanks_what: A word in braces, like {port}, is a blank filled in each time it runs. Leave a system empty and the command is not offered there.
beatbox.commands.for.only.what: Gone from the library of every other.
beatbox.watchers.about: Commands that keep running inside {name}, again and again, and tell you when their answer is news. They keep watching with this window closed, and only while {name} is running.
beatbox.watchers.machine_off: {name} is off, so its watchers are waiting. They go on when it starts.
beatbox.watchers.what: Commands with blanks are not offered: a watcher runs with nobody there to fill them. Nothing is installed inside the machine.
beatbox.commands.answer.mean: About {ms} ms each, there and back
beatbox.commands.answer.words: What it printed, word for word
beatbox.commands.what.processes: Every program running inside it, with a way to end one.
beatbox.commands.what.who: Who is signed in to it right now.
beatbox.commands.what.system: Which operating system it is, and which version.
beatbox.commands.what.uptime: How long since it last started.
beatbox.commands.what.disk: How full each of its disks is.
beatbox.commands.what.addresses: The addresses it has, on every network card.
beatbox.commands.what.ports: Which ports it waits on for connections.
beatbox.commands.what.routes: Where it sends traffic, and through what.
beatbox.commands.what.reach: Knocks four times and says how long each answer took.
beatbox.commands.what.resolve: Asks what address a name has, from inside it.
beatbox.commands.what.list: What is in a folder inside it, hidden files too.
beatbox.commands.what.read: The text of a file inside it.
beatbox.commands.what.downloads: The twenty newest files in its Downloads.
beatbox.watchers.said_none_on: Nothing watched on {name} has said anything yet.
beatbox.host.stopped_after_failed_restor: Going back to {name} failed, so the machine was turned off.
beatbox.host.state_saved: Its state was saved; the next start carries on from there.
